findings.reason: the gate would be green on the pre-fix tree exactly as the existing "changes no run row" cases are today, so the node's central measure would prove nothing.
findings.text: the done-when says the fixture is "seeded with one per-run record that still carries `follow_on_paths`" but never says that record must be one of the aggregate's own `runs` rows; `record_hold_checks` loads the aggregate (`reckon/ledger.py:3538`) and passes `payload["runs"]`, set from that aggregate's rows (`:2232`), to `_keep_run_files_identical` (`:2242`), which only rewrites rows it is handed and skips a row with no file — a record seeded the way `append_run` seeds one, as a file under `runs/` and not in the aggregate's list, is never visited, so the rewrite the first case asserts cannot happen and the case passes with the unfixed code

findings.reason: a §2 worker told where a site is must be able to open it, and five of the seven anchors point at code the deliverable does not name, so each has to be re-found by grep before the change can be scoped.
findings.text: every line anchor in the deliverable is mislocated, at the plan's own base commit a7e4578 as well as at head: `write` is at `reckon/ledger.py:2075` (cited 2007, which lands inside `_keep_run_files_identical`), `_keep_run_files_identical` at `:1967` (cited 1899, a blank line), its call at `:2242` (cited 2174, the fold-refusal `raise`), the `commit=True` gate at `:2203` and its `_commit_state_write` at `:2261` (cited 2192–2200 and 2135–2139, both the fold-refusal text), and `record_hold_checks` at `:3505` (cited 3440, inside a row-repair loop); the committing-caller anchors are worse because they land in different functions — `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3561` is the `--pretty` click option just above `def crew_verify_gate` with its `commit=True` at `:3678`, and `reckon/crew/routing.py:3006` is `_disposable_member_id` with the two `commit=True` calls at `:3054` and `:3181` (cited 3003 and 3130)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every ledger anchor in §2 is mislocated at both the plan's base revision and head, and the three committing-caller anchors land in unrelated functions (see FINDING anchors_resolve).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's first case rests on a seed that is not pinned to the aggregate's `runs` list, so it can pass on the unfixed code (see FINDING done_when).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are stated to sit under the run directory with the revision and literal command first and a bare `EXIT=` last, matching the sibling sections; no scratchpad path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 introduces one internal function and no public surface, and no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, path or comment it asks for.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence (a hold check rewrites per-run files through `_keep_run_files_identical` and commits only the aggregate path, `reckon/ledger.py:2242` → `:2261` → `:3609`), the cited inline comment does claim the run rows stay byte-identical (`:3536-3538`), `_commit_state_write` already accepts a set of paths for one commit (`:2506-2523`), and the production caller `reckon/budget.py:1911` resolves; the retired `follow_on_paths` spelling is normalised on read (`:1012-1018`), so a file carrying it is genuinely rewritten by a write that changed no run row.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — both deliverable changes serve the one goal in the heading, "a hold transition commits every run file it rewrote": the commit branch stops leaving run files behind, and the internal-function extraction is the mechanism that gives `record_hold_checks` the rewritten paths.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §2 is self-contained, declares no depends-on/informs/gates (`data-links=""` on the section, no plan-level graph), and its two write paths (`reckon/ledger.py`, `tests/test_hold_check_leaves_the_tree_clean.py`) are cited by no other section, so no missing or wrong edge.
